questions.stem: This schematic shows the synthesis of a vasodilating peptide from its precursor during inflammation. From which cells is this peptide primarily released?

explanation.summary: The diagram depicts bradykinin synthesis: kallikrein cleaves kininogen to yield bradykinin, causing vasodilatation. Like histamine, bradykinin is released mainly by mast cells and basophils during inflammation. Endothelial cells release NO and endothelin, atrial cardiomyocytes release ANP, and the posterior pituitary releases ADH.
